Offline embedding refresh jobs are scheduled batch processes that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus when the underlying embedding model changes or source documents update in bulk.

## Key Characteristics

**Execution Model**
- Runs on a fixed cadence rather than on demand
- Re-embeds the full or incremental document set as a batch operation
- Atomic swap of new vectors into the retrieval index to avoid serving mixed-model results during transition

**Operational Concerns**

- **Model versioning**: Embedding model version must be tracked per batch to enable auditing and rollback
- **Vector drift monitoring**: Detect and measure divergence between old and new embeddings to catch quality regressions early
- **Safe deployment**: Stage the swap behind a [[blue-green-deployment|blue/green index]] structure so that any quality regression can be rolled back without affecting live retrieval

## Rationale

By batching embedding regeneration on a schedule rather than performing ad hoc updates, systems can:
- Amortize the computational cost of re-embedding large corpora
- Coordinate model changes with infrastructure readiness
- Implement consistent change control across the embedding lifecycle
- Validate new embeddings before atomically swapping them into production

This pattern is particularly important when embedding models evolve (e.g., model upgrades, switching vendors, parameter tuning) or when source documents change in bulk (e.g., bulk ingestion, content migrations).
